attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The finite-matrix argument is valid, but Yang-Mills input is missing: a uniform reflected Wilson boundary OPE for q_\delta, identification of B_\delta without changing the locked algebra, and cutoff-removal control of the reflected products through the collar trace.
steps: Fix a finite locked Wilson collar family F_{1,\delta},...,F_{n,\delta}. Regulated reflection positivity and the closed-cone collar passage give a positive collar matrix N_\delta.
Separate additive contacts. A positive additive contact with zero diagonal vanishes by Cauchy-Schwarz; an indefinite or nonzero zero-diagonal contact is already a falsifier before quotienting.

Encode the remaining boundary discrepancy as a multiplicative Gram factor B_\delta. After diagonal normalization, same-theory OS positivity is the finite matrix condition q_\delta=\widehat N_\delta\oslash\widehat B_\delta\ge0.

For coincident-footprint hairpins, assume the boundary OPE gives q_\delta=J+\eta H+\eta^2K+\eta^3L+O(\eta^4). Pure one-body factors have the form h_i+\overline h_j and disappear from the zero-sum sector after the vacuum Schur step.
Apply the exact Schur complement along e. This gives T_\delta\ge0 as the exact test and yields A=PHP, B=P(K-n^{-1}Hee^*H)P, and the displayed third coefficient C.
If A has a negative zero-sum vector, q_\delta is indefinite for small \delta. If A is strictly positive on P\mathbb C^n, q_\delta is positive for small \delta with a uniform remainder.

If A\ge0 has kernel, take the Feshbach complement onto \ker A. The next coefficient is \Pi B\Pi; if it has a negative vector, this is the second-order mixed Wilson falsifier. On null directions of \Pi B\Pi, the next valid coefficient contains the correction -BA^\dagger B, not merely C.
Iterating gives a finite hierarchy: the first negative reduced coefficient produces a negative OS quadratic form; the first positive reduced coefficient with a gap promotes that finite block.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: No current RG estimate supplies the coefficients H,K,L and remainders for nonlocal Wilson hairpin blocks. Therefore the bridge is a sharp obstruction/proof gate, not yet OS positivity for continuum Yang-Mills.

assumptions: Regulated reflection positivity and RG convergence give N_\delta\ge0 for every fixed collar block.
Diagonal entries are positive and additive boundary contacts have either vanished by diagonal trace continuity or are separated as an earlier obstruction.
The multiplicative anomaly B_\delta is Hermitian with nonzero entries on the block, so the Hadamard quotient q_\delta is defined.
For coincident-footprint hairpins there is a uniform boundary OPE expansion q_\delta=J+\eta H+\eta^2K+\eta^3L+O(\eta^4), with \eta=\eta(\delta)\downarrow0.
The remainder is uniform on the finite block strongly enough that a spectral gap in the first nonzero reduced coefficient dominates it.
definitions: source object: finite regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms for locked gauge-invariant Wilson collar observables F_{i,\delta}, with continuum collar OS matrices N_\delta and multiplicative boundary Gram matrices B_\delta.

target object: OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions on the same locked gauge-invariant algebra, equivalently positive finite target matrices M_\delta=B_\delta^{[-1]}\circ N_\delta after diagonal normalization and collar trace.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions via finite reflected quadratic forms, Hadamard quotients q_\delta=\widehat N_\delta\oslash\widehat B_\delta, and closed-cone limits.

same-theory condition: the embeddings of Wilson collar observables into the continuum algebra are fixed before the limit; diagonal one-body renormalizations are allowed only as congruences, while pair-dependent boundary factors must pass q_\delta\ge0.
Here \widehat X_{ij}=X_{ij}/(X_{ii}X_{jj})^{1/2}, e=n^{-1/2}(1,\ldots,1), P=I-ee^*, and J_{ij}=1=n ee^*_{ij}.
The vacuum Schur complement removes the rank-one OS vacuum direction before testing mixed boundary OPE data.
A Feshbach reduced coefficient means the Schur complement onto the null space of the previous leading nonnegative coefficient.

equations.label: same-theory quotient
equations.valid_when: The boundary defect is multiplicative after diagonal normalization and no additive contact term remains hidden.

equations.label: rank-one boundary expansion
equations.valid_when: The reflected Wilson collars have a uniform coincident-footprint boundary OPE.

equations.label: exact vacuum Schur test
equations.latex: q_\delta\ge0\Longleftrightarrow e^*q_\delta e>0\ \text{ and }\ T_\delta:=Pq_\delta P-Pq_\delta e\,(e^*q_\delta e)^{-1}e^*q_\delta P\ge0
equations.valid_when: q_\delta is Hermitian and e^*q_\delta e>0, which holds for small \delta near J.

equations.label: first three Schur coefficients
equations.valid_when: The OPE expansion is valid through third order and e is the unit constant vector.

equations.label: first Feshbach reduction
equations.valid_when: A=PHP\ge0, \Pi is projection onto \ker A, and A has a positive spectral gap on (1-\Pi)P\mathbb C^n.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A negative value of c^*Ac, c^*\Pi B\Pi c, or c^*\Pi(C-BA^\dagger B)\Pi c at the first active level gives a concrete same-theory falsifier for that Wilson block.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: This lemma replaces vague Wilson boundary anomaly language by a finite-dimensional OS gate: compute H,K,L and the first nonzero Feshbach reduced form.
candidate_lemmas.statement: For a finite locked Wilson hairpin block whose normalized same-theory quotient q_delta tends to the rank-one vacuum matrix J, OS positivity after collar collapse is equivalent to positivity of an exact vacuum Schur complement. The first negative coefficient in its Feshbach hierarchy is a normalization-safe mixed boundary falsifier; if the first nonzero reduced coefficient is positive with a uniform remainder, the finite block is validly promoted.

assumptions: The cutoff-removal topology controls all finite reflected quadratic forms on the locked core.
The collar trace maps are same-theory maps, not boundary-renormalized algebra changes.
Finite-block positivity is stable under the core approximation seminorms.
definitions: OS-dense core: finite linear combinations of local mirror-flat gauge-invariant composites and mirror-smooth Wilson collars whose collar traces approximate the chosen test algebra in every finite reflected quadratic form.
uniform margin: the first nonzero reduced Feshbach coefficient on each finite block is positive by more than the stated OPE remainder.
closed OS cone: the set of Schwinger functionals with nonnegative finite reflected quadratic forms in the cutoff-removal topology.

equations.label: core approximation of OS forms
equations.valid_when: The approximation is in the initial topology generated by finite reflected OS quadratic forms.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If the Wilson core is not OS-dense or the topology misses reflected products, the finite quotient test may be valid but irrelevant to the intended theory.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Connects the finite Wilson obstruction calculation back to the global RG-to-OS bridge.
candidate_lemmas.statement: If the vacuum-Feshbach quotient test is satisfied with uniform margins on every block of an OS-dense locked Wilson core, and the local mirror-flat sector has the established trace modulus, then closedness of the OS cone extends reflection positivity from collars to the full continuum Schwinger family.

control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if H,K,L and remainders are computed on an OS-dense locked Wilson core and every first nonzero Feshbach reduced coefficient is positive or zero with a controlled next reduction.

falsifiers: First-order falsifier: a zero-sum vector c with c^*PHPc<0 for a realized Wilson hairpin block.
Second-order falsifier: A=PHP\ge0 but some c\in\ker A has c^*P(K-n^{-1}Hee^*H)Pc<0.
Third-order falsifier: on the reduced null space, c^*\Pi(C-BA^\dagger B)\Pi c<0; this detects mixed boundary OPE coupling to the positive first-order sector.
Additive-contact falsifier: a boundary contact matrix survives with zero diagonal but nonzero mixed entry, contradicting positive contact compatibility.
Topology falsifier: the cutoff-removal topology is valid for unreflected Wilson expectations but not for the reflected products defining N_\delta.
Same-theory falsifier: B_\delta is made positive only by adding a boundary counterterm or changing Wilson-loop renormalization at t=0.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 228 turns the Wilson boundary obstruction into an exact finite-matrix algorithm. The vacuum direction must be removed first by a Schur complement; then PHP, P(K-n^{-1}Hee^*H)P, and higher Feshbach reductions give normalization-safe tests. The valid falsifier is not a raw anomaly or PKP alone, but the first negative reduced coefficient after all rank-one and positive-sector couplings are eliminated. The remaining Yang-Mills work is now concrete: compute the reflected Wilson hairpin boundary OPE with uniform remainders.
